body:
Monarchs on the Move: Main Idea and Details: 1. Monarch butterflies make a very long migration each year, and it takes several generations to complete the round trip. 2. They glide on warm, rising air to save energy; they drink nectar for fuel and to store fat. 3. The fall monarchs that live up to eight months instead of two to six weeks; clues: "special," "can live for up to eight months," compared with "most monarchs live only two to six weeks." 4. Females lay eggs on milkweed, and it is the only plant monarch caterpillars can eat. 5. The butterflies that fly north do not finish the trip; their children and grandchildren keep going until a later generation reaches the starting place. 6. Summaries should include the long journey to Mexico, how they manage it, the super generation, the generations that return north, and the threats and help.
Two Accounts of the Monarch Journey: Sourcing: the journal is by a girl who tagged a butterfly with her aunt; she was there (she uses I and me, describes holding the butterfly). The article is a secondhand account by a writer who gathered facts; it gives numbers and general facts and no personal experience. Context: the journal is from September 14, in a meadow behind a nature center, when monarchs begin flying south. The article tells the distance, the super generation, the winter in Mexico and the return over generations, which the girl could not see. The journal tells what tagging feels like, how to tell a male, and how the sticker works. Claim: either choice; strong answers explain the different focus (one butterfly and one day versus the whole migration) and use a detail from each.
Reading Check: Why Leaves Change Color: 1. Leaves change color in autumn because trees stop making chlorophyll, which lets other colors show, before the leaves drop for winter. 2. A pigment, or coloring, that leaves use to make food from sunlight; clues: "a pigment, or coloring" and "make food from sunlight." 3. Trees stop making chlorophyll and it breaks down; the yellow and orange pigments were in the leaf all along and show when the green fades. 4. Sunny days and cool nights help some trees make more red pigment. 5. Example: shorter days and cooler nights (cause) make trees stop making chlorophyll (effect); or a layer of cells grows at the stem (cause) and the leaf drops (effect). 6. The summary names the green pigment, the fading in autumn, the yellow and red colors, and the leaf dropping.
Scoring tip: on the vocabulary criterion, a correct meaning without the clue words is Proficient; naming the clue words that gave the meaning is Advanced.
